p.modal-link: Where do I find the total amount of taxable interest?

modal-content.p: A 1099-INT is used by banks, financial institutions, government agencies, and other entities to report the amount of interest they paid to someone.
Depending on who issued it, 1099-INT forms may look different, but they should all have the name "Interest Income" on the form.
See an example 1099-INT
In most cases, if you received or more in interest , you should get a 1099-INT from the payer by January 31, .
Even if you didn’t get a 1099-INT, you’re still required to report any amount of interest you received.

If you lost or never received your 1099-INT, ask for a copy from the institution or person that paid your interest. If you still haven’t received the missing form(s) by the end of February, call the IRS at for help.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What interest income types aren’t yet supported in Direct File?

modal-content.p: Direct File doesn’t support items from boxes 2, 6, 8–13, and 17 on the 1099-INT, or interest income that appears on a different form like 1099-OID or 1099-B.
You also can’t use Direct File to report the following situations:

ul.li: You’re claiming the interest exclusion under the Education Savings Bond Program on series EE or I U.S. savings bonds issued after 1989
You received interest from a seller-financed mortgage, and the buyer used the property as a personal residence
You received a 1099-INT for U.S. savings bond interest that includes an amount you reported in a previous tax year
You received, as a nominee, interest that actually belongs to someone else
You received a 1099-INT for interest on frozen deposits
You received a 1099-INT for interest on a bond you bought between interest payment dates
You’re reporting interest income less than the amount shown on the 1099-INT due to amortizable bond premium
You owned tax credit bonds and received a Form 1097-BTC or need to file Form 8912 to claim the tax credits
You’re reporting market discount as interest income
You received a 1099-INT with tax-exempt interest

modal-content.p: If any of these unsupported situations apply to you, you’ll need to file using another tool. Find other ways to file your taxes.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: Where do I find my copy of the 1099-INT?

modal-content.p: Your payer should send you a copy of your Form 1099-INT by the end of February.
If you lost or never received your 1099-INT, ask for a copy from the institution or person that paid your interest.
If you still haven’t received the missing form(s) by the end of February, call the IRS at for help.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What if you received interest as a nominee?

modal-content.p: Direct File can’t be used to report nominee interest yet. You must report all of your income to the IRS, even if you’re not able to do so with Direct File. Find other ways to file your taxes..
If you receive a Form 1099 for interest in your name that actually belongs to someone else, IRS considers you to be a nominee recipient of that interest.
If you received a Form 1099-INT that includes an amount you received as a nominee for the real owner, you can’t use Direct File.
Under the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA), foreign banks and other financial institutions report information to the IRS about their U.S. account holders.

If a 1099-INT has the FATCA filing requirement box checked, it means you hold a foreign account and may need to file one or more additional forms that are not supported by Direct File. You need to find another way to file.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What if you want to exclude interest income under the Education Savings Bond Program?

modal-content.p: You may be able to exclude from income all or part of the interest you receive on the redemption of certain series EE and I U.S. savings bonds if you redeemed them in the same year in which you paid qualified higher education expenses. This exclusion is known as the Education Savings Bond Program.
The exclusion requires filing Form 8815, which Direct File doesn’t support yet.
If you want to file Form 8815, consider other ways to file your taxes..
Investment expenses in box 5 aren’t currently deductible on tax returns.
We skip box 7, "Foreign country or U.S. territory," because we don’t need this information to calculate your taxes.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: Where do I find the total amount of taxable interest?

modal-content.p: Taxable interest can often be found on a statement from the bank, financial institution, government agency, or other entity or person that paid your interest. You can also reach out directly to this entity for more information.
